name: @tylerschloesser/cdk-core
description: CDK constructs for PR-previewed, Google-authed personal sites
//: The subpath exports are the contract every consumer and every later epoch builds on. `.` is CDK-only (synth time, needs aws-cdk-lib); `./auth/browser` is DOM-only; `./auth/server` is Node-only. Keeping them apart is what lets a browser bundle import auth without pulling in aws-cdk-lib.

scripts.build: tsc -b && esbuild src/handlers/preview-resources.ts --bundle --platform=node --target=node22 --format=cjs --outfile=dist/handlers/preview-resources/index.js && echo '{"type":"commonjs"}' > dist/handlers/preview-resources/package.json && esbuild src/bin/sweep.ts --bundle --platform=node --target=node22 --format=cjs --outfile=dist/bin/sweep.js --banner:js='#!/usr/bin/env node' && echo '{"type":"commonjs"}' > dist/bin/package.json
scripts.//prepare: Runs `build` on every install. Two reasons, both load-bearing: pnpm only creates the `cdk-core` bin link for a workspace consumer if the bin target already exists at install time, and `dist/bin/sweep.js` is a build artifact — without this, `pnpm exec cdk-core sweep` in a fresh clone (every CI job) fails with `Command "cdk-core" not found`. It also means `npm publish` builds before packing.
